answer.short: Year 2: interest $\$100$; ending balance $\$1200$. Year 3: starting balance $\$1200$; interest $\$100$; ending balance $\$1300$. Year 4: starting balance $\$1300$; interest $\$100$; ending balance $\$1400$.
answer.worked:
The interest each year is calculated on the original $\$1000$.
$$1000\times0.1=100$$
Year 2: starting balance $\$1100$; interest $\$100$; ending balance $\$1100$ + $\$100$ = $\$1200$.
Year 3: starting balance $\$1200$; interest $\$100$; ending balance $\$1200$ + $\$100$ = $\$1300$.
Year 4: starting balance $\$1300$; interest $\$100$; ending balance $\$1300$ + $\$100$ = $\$1400$.

Interest earned = ending balance − principal.
$$1400-1000=400$$
The interest earned is $\$400$.

answer.worked:
Each year's interest is 10% of that year's starting balance.
Year 2:
$$\begin{aligned}1100\times0.1&=110\\1100+110&=1210\end{aligned}$$
Year 3:
$$\begin{aligned}1210\times0.1&=121\\1210+121&=1331\end{aligned}$$
Year 4:
$$\begin{aligned}1331\times0.1&=133.10\\1331+133.10&=1464.10\end{aligned}$$
The starting balances for years 3 and 4 are $\$1210$ and $\$1331$ respectively.

Interest earned = ending balance − principal.
$$1464.10-1000=464.10$$
The interest earned is $\$464.10$.
